sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Lada** ​(*lada*) ‌— Love, ‌Beauty, ​Spring ​· ​Lady, ​order — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Slavic tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Love, ​Beauty, ​Spring". The ​name ‌means ​"Lady, ‌order".

**Lada** ​is ‌love, ​beauty, ‌spring. ​The name ‌means ​"Lady, ​order" ‌and belongs ‌to ‌the ​slavic ​tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores ​the ​name ‌as ​**Lada** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/lada/). ​The ​restoration ​needs ‌no distinctive ‌letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​2. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*lada* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
No ​indigenous ‌written attestation ‌survives ​for ​this name; ​**Lada** ​is ​a scholarly ‌transliteration ​of ​the ‌reconstructed spoken ​form. ‌Etymologically ​the name ‌means ​"Lady, ​order".

​The ASCII ​form ​*lada* ‌survives only ​because ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system ​could ‌not ​carry diacritics; ‌it ​is ​a technological ‌compromise, ‌not ‌an ​ancient spelling. ​The ‌Unicode ​restoration **Lada** ​recovers ‌the ​full diacritic ​detail ‌of ​the ‌scholarly transliteration ​directly ​in ​the address ​bar. ‌The ‌restoration needs ​no ‌distinctive ​letters ​or diacritics ‌its ‌ASCII ‌form would ‌lose, ​which ‌places ​the name ​in ​Tier ‌2.

The ​letter-by-letter ​transformation ​runs:

- ‌**l** ​→ ​**L** ​— Same, ‌capitalized
​- ‌**a** → ​**a** ‌— ​Same
‌- **d** ‌→ ​**d** ​— Same
​- ​**a** ‌→ **a** ‌— ​Same

sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/lada/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**lada** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Lada.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"lada" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Lada".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"lada" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Lada" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Lada was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Lada ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Lada ‌place ​love, beauty, ​spring ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

‌### Origins ​(Myth)

‌Lada appears ​in ‌slavic ​tradition as ​love, ​beauty, spring. ​The ​name's ‌meaning, "Lady, ​order", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### ‌Worship and ​Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​Lada ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name ​survived into ‌the ​modern scholarly ‌record.

​The ​myths of ​Lada ​survive in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ​Each ​version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ‌tellers ​— poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex entry ​does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Lada ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Lada ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Slavic ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Lada, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​love ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Lada is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of love, ​Beauty, ‌Spring ​in ​the ‌mind and ​to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Lady, order" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​love, ‌Beauty, ​Spring ​· ‌Lady, order.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Lada ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*lada* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
